pattern_title: Authorization code and facility mapping issues are masking true spend trends
pattern_description: A large share of the observed increase is tied to authorization code distribution shifts and claims sitting in Not Mapped facility buckets. That means part of the signal may be administrative reclassification rather than true utilization or provider performance change. Business action on prior authorization policy, provider economics, or site-of-care should wait until these records are validated and reclassified.

claims.summary: CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION contributed +$2.2M, led by Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC (+$0.7M) and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC (+$0.6M). VA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added +$1.0M. VA Not Mapped facility claims added +$375K on 25 more admissions, and GA Not Mapped added about +$180K across UTI and Ungroupable drivers. OH / PA Not Mapped added +$101K in small-volume, high-paid cases.

pattern_title: CA acute hospital spend is concentrated in three PPO Local providers
pattern_description: In CA PPO Local acute hospitals, spend is concentrated in three providers with two distinct drivers. UCI Medical Center and Huntington Health are mainly seeing more admissions, while Hoag Hospital Newport Beach shows both more admissions and higher paid per admit. This is a targeted provider-mix issue inside one product and facility setting, not a broad statewide pricing jump.

claims.summary: UCI Medical Center added +$0.6M with 27 more admissions, while paid per admit fell by about $0.4K. Huntington Health added +$0.5M with 23 more admissions and largely flat paid per admit. Hoag Hospital Newport Beach added +$0.7M with 24 more admissions and paid per admit up about $3.6K. UTI and nervous system DRGs were recurring drivers, each adding about +$87K to +$140K.

pattern_title: CA complex IP Med/Surg admissions are driving a concentrated inpatient spike
pattern_description: CA IP Med/Surg growth is being driven by a narrow set of complex sepsis, neurologic, respiratory failure, and UTI-related admissions rather than a broad inpatient trend. Some of the dollars reflect repeatable volume and intensity growth, while a meaningful share comes from very rare, very high-cost stays. This should be managed as a focused inpatient case-mix issue with both clinical and UM review.

claims.summary: CA IP Med/Surg new or rare high-cost cases added +$0.8M, including a tracheostomy/mechanical ventilation case at Huntington Health (+$131K) and sepsis with major O.R. procedures at UCI Medical Center (+$103K). CA IP Med/Surg volume and intensity added +$0.8M, led by UTI site not specified (+$261K on 31 more admissions) and critical illness myopathy (+$160K). Sepsis without prolonged ventilation added another +$95K at Hoag Hospital Newport Beach with 5 more admissions and paid per admit up about $1.6K. Several rare drivers carried paid per admit from about $45K to $131K.

pattern_title: CA post-acute spend is rising across SNF, rehab, and NF
pattern_description: CA post-acute spend rose across SNF - FREE STANDING, Physical Rehab, and NF. The pattern combines more post-acute volume with higher paid per admit in key SNF and rehab cells, plus a nursing-facility case mix weighted to neurologic, sepsis, cellulitis, and UTI cases. This points to a broader discharge and post-acute management opportunity rather than a single-provider issue.

claims.summary: CA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.6M across volume and mixed-cost groups, including 19 more admissions in one major driver and paid per admit up about $4.9K to $7.6K in key SNF cells. CA Physical Rehab added +$211K on 5 more admissions with paid per admit up about $9.1K. CA NF new or rare cases added +$257K, including anoxic brain damage and sepsis-related ungroupable stays. CA NF volume and intensity added +$166K, including cellulitis of left lower limb (+$97K) and other toxic encephalopathy (+$70K).

pattern_title: OH and PA spend is concentrated in Lehigh Valley and Lee Memorial, with a high-cost inpatient tail
pattern_description: OH and PA spend is concentrated in Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest and Lee Memorial Hospital, with more acute admissions and a smaller but meaningful tail of high-cost cardiac, respiratory, and sepsis cases. OH is more volume-led, while PA shows clearer paid-per-admit pressure at Lehigh Valley. This is best handled as a targeted provider and case-mix issue rather than a broad market-wide response.

claims.summary: OH acute hospital PPO Local added +$0.5M, led by Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest (+$211K) and Lee Memorial Hospital (+$117K) on 17 and 12 more admissions. PA acute hospital spend at Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest added +$305K with 10 more admissions and paid per admit up about $6.2K. OH / PA rare IP Med/Surg cases added +$306K, including cardiac surgery for non-ST elevation myocardial infarct (+$95K) and heart failure or ventilator-supported respiratory failure cases. PA SNF - FREE STANDING added +$69K with 9 more admissions.

pattern_title: VA costs are rising across the inpatient-to-SNF continuum
pattern_description: In VA, the same PPO Local population shows higher spend in both acute hospitals and SNF - FREE STANDING. Acute growth is mostly more admissions, while SNF adds both more admissions and higher paid per admit, pointing to rising costs across the inpatient-to-post-acute continuum. This suggests the management opportunity sits across discharge planning and post-acute utilization, not just inpatient authorization.

claims.summary: VA acute hospital PPO Local added +$0.7M with 46 more admissions and essentially flat paid per admit. VA SNF - FREE STANDING added +$0.4M with 37 more admissions and paid per admit up about $1.2K. Both increases sit in auth-required services, indicating broader utilization pressure across the care continuum.

pattern_title: GA shows a recurring cellulitis and UTI pathway problem across acute and post-acute care
pattern_description: GA shows a coherent cellulitis and UTI story across acute hospital, Physical Rehab, IP Med/Surg, and NF. The largest dollars come from acute hospital admissions, but the same diagnoses recur in clinical case-mix groups, suggesting avoidable admission and post-acute pathway opportunities rather than isolated noise. This pattern should be worked through diagnosis-specific clinical and UM action.

claims.summary: GA acute hospital PPO Local added +$0.4M, led by Cellulitis without MCC (+$213K on 28 more admissions) and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC (+$206K on 25 more admissions). GA IP Med/Surg cellulitis cases added +$241K, including left lower limb (+$125K) and right lower limb (+$90K), with paid per admit up about $2.3K. GA Physical Rehab added +$150K on 7 more admissions. GA NF cellulitis cases added about +$78K across left lower limb and face.

pattern_title: Small-market and low-volume outliers need case-by-case triage, not broad policy action
pattern_description: Several smaller segments show emerging outliers, but each is based on low volume and should be handled as a targeted exception. The mix includes small-market SNF pressure, isolated acute hospital spikes, a ME critical access increase, and two one-case craniotomy stroke admissions in CA / PA. These are important to triage, but they do not yet support broad utilization, reimbursement, or network changes.

claims.summary: Small-market SNF pressure added +$159K across IN / ME / OH, with paid per admit up about $2.5K to $5.6K. CT / IN / NY acute hospital outliers added +$149K, including a 1-admission ungroupable CT case of +$55K. ME CRITICAL ACCESS added +$44K from 2 admissions with paid per admit about $21.8K higher. CA / PA craniotomy stroke cases added +$119K across 2 one-admission cases at UCI Medical Center and Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest.
